newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi television shows Uday improving.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi television shows Uday improving.

text.p: Fresh television images showed Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday looking stronger than in the first pictures released after an apparent assassination attempt.

The pictures late on Friday on Shabab television, a channel run by Uday, showed him relaxed and shaking hands with visitors to his hospital room -- seemingly in better health than when television pictures were first shown 10 days ago.
Uday was reported shot and wounded by unidentified gunmen on December 12 as he was driving in Baghdad's wealthy district of al-Mansour.

On television, Uday shook hands with a Sudanese youth delegation and heads of the Iraqi students and youth unions and senior ruling Baath party officials while lying on his bed in Ibn Sina hospital in Baghdad.

Iraq has made no official comment on the identity of the attackers or whether they were still at large. Uday, speaking to a reporter from the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) a few days after the attempt on his life. blamed Iran -- which denied the charge.

Two Iraqi opposition groups abroad claimed responsibility and gave different versions on the attack. The Iraqi goverment gave no details of the attack apart from a newspaper report saying several other people were seriously wounded.
Uday is chairman of Iraq's National Olympic Committee, owns the newspaper Babel, Iraq's most influential, and runs the popular Shabab television channel.

Celebrations were reported continuing across the country for Uday's survival. Newspapers said there were daily events at the spot where Uday was attacked, with food distributed free to those attending.
The newspapers also said festivities were held on Friday at Baghdad al-Shaab (people) Stadium organised by the Iraqi Olympic Committee.
